stem: In a code, each letter is replaced by the letter that occupies the mirror-image position in the alphabet. That is, A (1st from the start) is coded as Z (1st from the end), B (2nd from start) is coded as Y (2nd from end), and so on (positions always sum to 27). Using this rule, what is the code for STAMP?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Mirror rule (positions sum to 27): S(19)->H(8), T(20)->G(7), A(1)->Z(26), M(13)->N(14), P(16)->K(11), giving HGZNK.
Mistakenly coding A as A (forgetting that A mirrors to Z since 1+26=27) gives HGANK with A in the third position unchanged.
Misidentifying the pattern as a fixed +8 shift (since S+8 wraps to A) and applying it uniformly gives ABIUX, not the mirror result.
Using mirror positions that sum to 26 instead of 27 (an off-by-one error throughout) gives S->G, T->F, A->Y, M->M(?), P->J, producing GFYMJ.

explanation: The mirror rule: if a letter occupies position p from the start, its code occupies position p from the end, so original_pos + coded_pos = 27. Apply to STAMP: S(19)->H(8), T(20)->G(7), A(1)->Z(26), M(13)->N(14), P(16)->K(11) = HGZNK. Verify: 19+8=27, 20+7=27, 1+26=27, 13+14=27, 16+11=27.

explanation_sections.punchline: The mirror rule pairs letters whose positions sum to 27, not 26 - this off-by-one is the decisive trap.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: state the rule precisely (pos1 + pos2 = 27), then compute each pair for STAMP. A quick check: does A map to Z (1+26=27) or Y (1+25=26)? The stem confirms Z, so 27 is the sum.
explanation_sections.lesson: For mirror-alphabet codes, always verify whether positions sum to 27 (A<->Z) or 26 (A<->Y) before solving.
explanation_sections.timing: About 75-85 seconds. Fastest elimination: option 3 has A as a mid-letter coded as I (a +8 shift) which contradicts the mirror framing entirely.
